name: Choppa
notes: Triggerman bounce with nothing else on top — the most reduced model in this batch, and the fastest. ⛔ **"Often one chord for the whole record — bounce's harmonic norm."** So `maxChords` is 2, the tonic family carries weight 8 against 1 and 1, and `chords.impliedByRiff` is set because the keyboard riff is the only thing stating a chord. The variety a static harmony would otherwise cost is bought with a 4–16 beat `chordDurationBeats`, three `harmonicRhythm` values and the widest `voicing.register` in this batch — what varies on these records is how long the loop sits, not what it sits on. The two non-tonic families are **INFERRED** and carry weight 1 each; they are the first thing to delete if this ever sounds busier than "Choppa Style" does. ⛔ **"Extremely low note density"**, so `melody.densityPerBar` is 2–5 with `motifPitchCount` 2–4 and `emptyBarBias` 0.2 — the sparsest melody here alongside `mystikal`, and for the opposite reason: Mystikal empties the bar for a shout, this empties it for a dance call-out. `timbreHint` is `square_lead` for the whistle, which is the same substitution the parent documents — the dataset names no whistle voice and `square_lead` is the nearest it has. ⛔ **`drums.bass808.role` flips to `bassline`.** "808 sub locked to the kick; **no melodic bass**" is unambiguous: the parent's played Moog is switched off entirely, and the 808 is the whole low end with `slideProb` at 0.02. This is the strongest case for the flip anywhere in the batch. ⛔ **The Triggerman cell is at full strength:** `offSnare.prob` 0.95 (the snare answer *is* the grammar), the highest `kick.syncopation` and `tresilloBias` here, cowbell 8ths with clave and rim for the chromatic "tics", and `percs.gainOffsetDb` at -1. ⛔ **"Sections marked by drop-outs rather than chord changes; 4- and 8-bar chant blocks instead of 16-bar verses."** That is the arrangement, literally: `verse` reaches only 4 and 8, `dropOutBeats.prob` is 0.9 — the highest in this batch — and `switchUpProb` falls to 0.04 because the record is a continuous loop. ⚠ **Confidence `medium`, matching the research**, which sources the bounce grammar and his place in it but marks the 95–105 band **[LOW-CONF on the band]**. Inferred: the key list, every velocity and register bound, `intervals`/`contour`, and the two non-tonic chord families. ⚠ The shouted "break" marker has no lane and is not faked. ⚠ `snareRoll.pitchWalk` is inherited. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 45 to 43 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 44 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 2. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2,4], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 970/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [2,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 972/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.2 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 972/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
